name: code_engraved_in_the_center
why: The benchmark: «PROVA» 10 mm high engraved 2 mm on a face that contains all of it. It is the case the refusals lean on, and without it «does not fit» would not tell a check that works from one that refuses everything.
_why_the_area_and_not_the_volume: The area of the letters cannot be calculated from the string: it depends on the font. But the removed volume divided by the depth gives it, and that number is stable. It is the only way to have an expectation that is not «different from zero» -- which would pass even on an inscription cut off halfway.

expect.why: «PROVA» has 56 outlines: each letter its outer one, and P, R, O, A also the inner one. It is the number that says the letters were really built and that the operation did not just read a string.

expect.tolerance_why: the width comes from the drawing of the glyphs of the font, and the last digit depends on the sampling of the curves: below a tenth of a millimetre it is not a number to lean on
same reason; and the box is taller than the 10 mm asked because «PROVA» has no letters that go below the line, but the glyphs stick out slightly
the volume of an engraving is the sum of 56 curved outlines: half a cubic millimetre is the tessellation noise, not a variation
it is the volume divided by two, so half of the tolerance above

expect.why: a marking must not detach anything

expect.tolerance_why: it is the same number as above seen from the other side: the volume of the part, read from the state instead of from the answer of the operation

expect.why: this face is a full square, so the check «it fits in the box» is complete -- and the operation says so instead of letting it be believed
